llm.summary: This Obsidian note skill has a coherent purpose, but it overreaches by reading agent memory and automatically pushing broad local repository changes to network destinations.

dimensions.detail: The declared read/write/exec/memory_search authority is broad for a note skill, and scripts perform network calls, broad filesystem reads, and Git operations with limited path or destination validation.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation uses npx clawhub@latest plus a manual git clone/link path; this is not malicious by itself but is unpinned and less reproducible than a reviewed exact version.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime prompts include Git push as a normal processing step, README describes handling any WhatsApp or Telegram message, and there is no clear per-run confirmation boundary before remote synchronization.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill declares scheduled agents and Git backup enabled by default, and sync scripts commit/push into persistent repository history; the scripts also silently run openclaw doctor --fix-zombies, which is unrelated process management.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Voice/chat note capture, Obsidian writes, Ollama search, and Git backup fit the stated purpose, but the search script also indexes ~/.openclaw/workspace/memory and the sync scripts push the entire Obsidian repository rather than only generated notes.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only after reviewing and constraining the paths, disabling or gating automatic Git push, confirming the remote repository is private and intended, changing Ollama to a trusted local loopback endpoint, and removing OpenClaw memory from the default search paths.
llm.findings:
[T05] unexpected: Confirmed: search_engine.py includes ~/.openclaw/workspace/memory in the indexed paths even though the advertised semantic-search scope is Obsidian notes.
[T09] unexpected: Confirmed: search_engine.py posts queries and note or memory excerpts to a default plaintext HTTP endpoint at 192.168.3.120; Ollama embeddings are expected, but this non-loopback default and memory scope are under-disclosed.
[T09] expected: Confirmed: push_to_git.sh and sync.sh run git add -A, commit, and git push origin; Git backup is advertised, but staging all changes/deletions without review or secret scanning is overbroad.
[T05] unexpected: Confirmed: the Git sync scripts silently invoke openclaw doctor --fix-zombies after sync, which is unrelated to Obsidian note backup and suppresses output.
[T08] expected: Confirmed: the documented npx clawhub@latest installer is unpinned; this is a supply-chain hygiene issue rather than evidence of malicious behavior.
[TT3] expected: Downgraded as framed: OLLAMA_BASE_URL is an endpoint setting rather than a credential, but the same code still creates a material note-content network disclosure risk.
[TP4] expected: Partially accepted: GitHub/Git backup is mentioned in the skill, but automatic broad staging and pushing creates an expectation gap for a privacy-focused notes workflow.
[TM1] expected: Partially accepted: git push is explicitly part of the workflow; git reset --hard and git push --force appear as prohibited examples, so the material issue is automatic remote push rather than those forbidden commands.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Accepted: the scripts claim a 'only add, never delete' safety property while git add -A can stage deletions, and privacy claims of local-only operation conflict with GitHub sync and a non-loopback Ollama endpoint.
[SQP-2] expected: Accepted in part: backup and scheduled agents fit the product concept, but the artifacts do not clearly require opt-in, review, or destination confirmation before unattended writes and remote sync.
[LP3] expected: Accepted in part: exec/read/write/memory_search are understandable for this workflow, but their scope is not narrowed to the Obsidian vault or safe Git operations.
[RA2] expected: Downgraded: the cited GitHub repository creation guide is release documentation, not evidence of hidden session persistence.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded for this security verdict: the Chinese-language documentation is coherent with the package audience and does not by itself show unsafe behavior.
